Thought: Looking at the proton NMR spectrum, I don't see any characteristic signals for methyl groups, which typically appear as a singlet around 0.9-2.5 ppm. The signals at 1.35 ppm are part of a more complex splitting pattern (dtt) with 10H, suggesting they are part of a cyclic system rather than methyl groups. The other signals at 2.63 and in the aromatic region (7.24 and 7.41) also don't correspond to methyl groups.

Let me confirm this by checking the carbon NMR spectrum.
Action: carbon_nmr_spectra
Action Input: {}

Thought: The carbon NMR spectrum confirms there are no methyl groups in the molecule. Methyl carbons typically appear in the range of 15-30 ppm, and while there are signals in this region (26.90, 26.18), these correspond to CH2 groups in the cyclic system rather than CH3 groups, as evidenced by the proton NMR coupling patterns we saw earlier. The other carbon signals are either aromatic carbons (147.00, 133.90, 128.91, 127.68) or aliphatic CH/CH2 carbons (44.06, 34.54).
